Question: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) and \(d\) be the lengths of sides \(MN,\) \(NP,\) \(PQ\) and \(QM,\) respectively, of quadrilateral \(MNPQ.\) If \(A\) is the area of \(MNPQ,\) then

Choices.A:
\(A=\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is convex
Choices.B:
\(A=\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if and
only if \(MNPQ\) is a rectangle
Choices.C:
\(A\le\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is a rectangle
Choices.D:
\(A\le\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is a parallelogram
Choices.E:
\(A\ge\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right)\) if
and only if \(MNPQ\) is a parallelogram

Solution:
A triangle with two side lengths \(u,v\) has area at most \(uv/2\): use \(u\) as its base, and its height is at most \(v\). Equality holds precisely when those two sides are perpendicular. Applying this observation along both diagonals will involve all four corners of the quadrilateral.

Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). Using diagonal \(MP\) gives
\[
A\le [MNP]+[MPQ]\le\frac{ab+cd}{2}.
\]
Using diagonal \(NQ\) gives
\[
A\le [MNQ]+[NPQ]\le\frac{ad+bc}{2}.
\]
These estimates also cover concave quadrilaterals: when a diagonal lies outside the quadrilateral, its area is the absolute difference of the two triangle areas, which is smaller than their sum.

Adding the bounds and dividing by \(2\), we obtain
\[
A\le\frac{ab+cd+ad+bc}{4}
=\frac{(a+c)(b+d)}4.
\]
If equality holds here, both original bounds must be equalities. A concave quadrilateral is therefore excluded. A collinear corner would also make a triangle bound strict. Equality in the first triangulation forces right angles at \(N\) and \(Q\); equality in the second forces right angles at \(M\) and \(P\). Thus the quadrilateral is a rectangle.

Conversely, a rectangle has \(a=c\), \(b=d\), and area \(ab\), so
\[
A=ab=\left(\frac{a+c}{2}\right)
\left(\frac{b+d}{2}\right).
\]
Both directions hold, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
